ov: Tiny arachnids, mostly under 1 mm, with eight legs and a simple, unsegmented body. Many live in soil as decomposers, others on plants, and some are predators or parasites, such as the Varroa mite of honey bees and the scabies mite of humans. Most are harmless to people.
len: Mostly under 1 mm; face mites 0.3–0.4 mm
rg: Worldwide, in soil, water, on plants and on animals.
df: Varies widely: decaying matter, plants, other small animals, or the skin and blood of hosts.
fx: Face mites leave the hair follicles at night and walk around on the skin at 8–16 mm an hour.
In one 2014 study, every one of 19 adults tested carried face mites.
notes: RESOLVED (owner approved all suggestions, 2026-09-29; h left unchanged for bumblebee, hornet and firefly): Group entry. The fact is confirmed: two Demodex species live in human hair follicles, "primarily found in the face", and their presence "is common and usually does not cause any symptoms".
